name: HDC3022 temperature & humidity sensor
description: Texas Instruments digital temperature (-40 to 125 °C, ±0.1 °C typical) and relative humidity (0–100 %, ±0.5 % typical) sensor with an I2C interface, CRC-checked data and a dust/water-resistant PTFE filter cover. Runs on 1.8–5.5 V with no regulator, so logic levels follow VIN. Sold as: Adafruit HDC3022 Precision Temperature & Humidity Sensor - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (product 5989; 6-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, RST, ALERT), I2C address 0x44 (0x45–0x47 with the A0/A1 jumpers on the back), 10 kΩ pull-ups on SDA/SCL.
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is, very accurately, through a little filter that keeps dust and splashes out.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 1.8–5.5 V (no regulator: use the same voltage as your board's logic, 3.3 V)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: RST
pins.description: Reset input, active low (internal ~49 kΩ pull-up); leave unconnected for basic use

pins.name: ALERT
pins.description: Push-pull alert/interrupt output for threshold alerts, not needed for basic use

supplierQuery: Adafruit HDC3022 temperature humidity sensor STEMMA QT 5989
buildNotes: Trigger-on-demand command 0x24 0x00 (low power mode 0), then wait at least 12.5 ms before reading 6 bytes: temperature MSB, LSB, CRC, humidity MSB, LSB, CRC. Reading too early is NACKed.
Check each CRC (CRC-8 poly 0x31, init 0xFF; 0xABCD gives 0x6F). A mismatch almost always means a loose SDA/SCL wire.
Default address 0x44; close the A0 jumper for 0x45, A1 for 0x46, both for 0x47.
Do not remove the white PTFE filter cover; peel off the protective sticker if one is fitted.
Keep the sensor away from the microcontroller and regulators, which warm the air around them.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from hdc3022 import HDC3022

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = HDC3022(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
